description:
## Contract risk

calendars-client `calendar_set`, `calendar_event_set`, and `participant_identity_set` take:

- `create: Option<HashMap<String, FooType>>`  (typed)
- `destroy: Option<&[Id]>`                    (borrowed slice)

Canonical mail-client (workspace AGENTS.md + crate-jmap-mail-client/AGENTS.md
both name jmap-mail-client as the canonical extension-client template) uses:

- `create: Option<serde_json::Value>`  (untyped)         crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/email.rs:106
- `destroy: Option<Vec<Id>>`           (owned)          crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/email.rs:108

Same shapes recur in `mailbox_set` and `identity_set`.

## Why this matters for a caller

A caller wiring up jmap-mail-client and jmap-calendars-client in the same app
sees two different Rust patterns for the same underlying JMAP concept:

```rust
sc_mail.email_set(Some(json!({...})), None, Some(vec![id]), None).await?;
sc_cal.calendar_set(Some(hashmap), None, Some(&[id][..]), None).await?;
```

The typed-HashMap create map also locks in the wire-shape defect already filed
as JMAP-1j9k.1 (every `Calendar` value carries a required `id` field that gets
serialized into the create-map value, violating RFC 8620 §5.3). The canonical
untyped `serde_json::Value` create lets the caller construct create-map values
that omit `id` properly.

The borrowed `&[Id]` destroy forces the caller to keep the `Vec<Id>` alive
across the `.await` point. The canonical `Vec<Id>` takes ownership. For
composed async code this matters in practice.

## What goes wrong if this stays

Once shipped at 0.x.y, the divergence is locked in: changing `create` from
`Option<HashMap<String, Calendar>>` to `Option<serde_json::Value>` and
`destroy` from `Option<&[Id]>` to `Option<Vec<Id>>` are both breaking changes
requiring a major version bump and migration on every caller.

Per the workspace canonical-template propagation rule, the divergence is
itself the regression — either jmap-mail-client should change to match the
calendars typed-map shape (with all six other extension-client siblings
sweeping in the same pass), or calendars-client should change to match the
canonical. The current state is a divergent sibling without a matching change
to the canonical, which the workspace AGENTS.md explicitly calls out as
"a regression of the cookie-cutter intent".

## Fix shape

Option A (preferred per canonical-template rule): change calendars-client to
match the canonical untyped shapes.

Option B: change jmap-mail-client first and propagate to all siblings.

Either way, no API contract decision should ship in 0.x.y until the
workspace-level decision is recorded somewhere (PLAN.md or a workspace-design
bead) so all siblings stay aligned.
